backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS, use a distribution of radii that is biased towards larger values (e.g., the highest possible sum of 26 radii that could fit in a unit square) or a random power-law distribution.
backlog.title: Multi-start SLSQP with Better Initial Radii

backlog.spec: Adjust MAX_ITER based on the remaining time in the solve loop, ensuring that the final iteration of the 80% time budget is the last one processed.
backlog.title: Dynamic MAX_ITER

backlog.spec: Provide an explicit analytical Jacobian for the constraints in the minimize function to improve the accuracy and speed of the gradient calculations.
backlog.title: Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) with custom Jacobian

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function to iteratively reduce radii by a factor of 0.999 until no overlaps exist, rather than a fixed 50 iterations.
backlog.title: Iterative Radius Shrinking Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of hard constraints in SLSQP, use a penalty function approach where overlaps and boundary violations are added to the objective function with a large weight.
backlog.title: Soft Penalty Method

backlog.spec: Use Simulated Annealing to explore the space of radii and centers, only switching to SLSQP when the configuration is nearly valid and the temperature is low.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing Restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the random initialization with a greedy approach where circles are placed one by one in the 'best' available spots before calling minimize.
backlog.title: Greedy Initialization

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP call, perform a brief local search (e.g., 100 steps of coordinate descent) to wiggle the circles and increase the sum of radii.
backlog.title: Local Search refinement

backlog.spec: Implement a simple physics-based 'shaking' step where circles are pushed away from each other and the boundaries, then let them settle.
backlog.title: Velocity-based Repulsion

backlog.spec: In the _repair function, adjust the shrinkage factor based on the magnitude of the overlap: larger overlaps result in more significant shrinkage.
backlog.title: Adaptive Shrinkage

backlog.spec: Initialize circle centers such that they are biased towards the corners and edges, as this is often where optimal packings have high density.
backlog.title: Boundary-aware Initialization

backlog.spec: Sort the radii in descending order before the optimization. This helps the optimizer focus on fitting the largest circles first, which are harder to place.
backlog.title: Pre-sorted Radii

backlog.spec: Use a multi-stage optimization: start with a low penalty for overlaps and gradually increase the penalty weight to force the solution into a valid state.
backlog.title: Gradual Penalty Increase

backlog.spec: Optimize centers and radii in separate stages, or use a block-diagonal approach to optimize groups of circles at once.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise SLSQP

backlog.spec: When restarting the optimization, jitter the best found configuration slightly (e.g., move centers by 0.01) instead of starting completely from scratch.
backlog.title: Jittered Restart

backlog.spec: Optimize for the log of the radii to ensure they stay positive and to change the sensitivity of the optimizer to small vs large radii.
backlog.title: Log-space Radii

backlog.spec: If a circle's radius falls below a certain threshold (e.g., 0.001), remove it from the optimization and focus on the remaining circles.
backlog.title: Hard-coded Small Circle Removal

backlog.spec: Initialize the circles in a hexagonal packing grid and then 'squash' them into the unit square before starting the optimization.
backlog.title: Tiling Initialization

backlog.spec: Use the result of a failed (invalid) SLSQP run as the starting point for a second run with tighter constraints or a smaller step size.
backlog.title: Penalty-based SLSQP Warm Start

backlog.spec: Allocate a larger portion of the time limit to the most promising runs (those that achieve a higher sum of radii) and less to poor runs.
backlog.title: Dynamic Time Budgeting

backlog.spec: Use a smooth approximation of the boundary constraints (e.g., a sigmoid or a high-power polynomial) to keep the gradient smoother.
backlog.title: Non-linear Boundary Constraints

backlog.spec: Since the harness is single-threaded, find a way to structure the logic so that multiple 'attempts' are processed as efficiently as possible within the time limit.
backlog.title: Parallelize Restarts

backlog.spec: Instead of optimizing radii directly, optimize a scaling factor for each circle's radius relative to a set of 'base' radii.
backlog.title: Radius Scaling

backlog.spec: In the repair step, use a SOR-like approach to adjust radii, which can converge faster than simple iterative shrinking.
backlog.title: Successive Over-Relaxation

backlog.spec: In the repair function, shrink radii by a random factor between 0.95 and 1.0 instead of a fixed amount to avoid local minima.
backlog.title: Randomized Shrinkage

backlog.spec: Temporarily treat circles as ellipses during the initial search to allow for easier packing, then 'round' them to circles in the final phase.
backlog.title: Elliptical Smoothing

backlog.spec: Manually implement a gradient clipping step if the SLSQP gradients become too large (e.g., during high-overlap states).
backlog.title: Gradient Clipping

backlog.spec: In the repair loop, identify the circle involved in the most overlaps and shrink it the most.
backlog.title: Better Repair Loop

backlog.spec: Optimize for two objectives: maximum sum of radii and minimum overlap, using a weighted sum.
backlog.title: Multi-Objective Optimization

backlog.spec: Monitor the progress of SLSQP and terminate the current call early if no significant improvement is made over X iterations, moving to the next restart.
backlog.title: Time-based Early Exit

backlog.spec: When a new packing is found that is better than the current best, use it as a starting point for a small 'jitter' and re-solve. Specifically, slightly perturb the centers (e.g., by a factor of 0.01) and allow the radii to vary freely in the next SLSQP call to escape local optima while staying in a high-quality basin.
backlog.title: Basin-Hopping Jittering

backlog.spec: If the sum of radii is not improving after several restarts, identify the smallest circle in the current best packing and remove it entirely. Re-run the optimization for n-1 circles. If the total radius increases (because the removed circle was very small and its removal allowed others to grow significantly), keep the new packing. Repeat this periodically.
backlog.title: Small Circle Removal

backlog.spec: Instead of starting from random radii, start with a known valid packing (like a grid) and use SLSQP to maximize the radii while keeping centers fixed. Then, perform a second phase where centers are allowed to move while radii are slowly increased. This 'expansion' approach often finds denser configurations than pure random starts.
backlog.title: Iterative Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: Calculate the average time taken per SLSQP call. Adjust MAX_ITER dynamically so that the script always utilizes exactly 80% of the time_limit, regardless of how fast or slow the individual optimization steps are.
backlog.title: Time-Proportional MAX_ITER

backlog.spec: Replace the current repair logic with a more aggressive iterative shrinker. In each step, find the circle pair with the maximum overlap and shrink both radii by a factor proportional to the overlap magnitude. Repeat until all overlaps are below 1e-11. This is often more stable than the current sum-based shrink.
backlog.title: Successive Shrinkage Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random radii, generate radii from a power-law distribution or a sorted list of $n$ values sampled from a range. Large circles are harder to place; placing them first (or biasing the solver to prefer larger radii) can improve the final sum.
backlog.title: Pre-sorted Radius Initialization

backlog.spec: Instead of just one elliptical stretch, use a sequence of 3 stretches (e.g., 0.8, 1.0, 1.2) as successive starting points in a single `_solve_once` call. The solution of the first becomes the start of the second, and so on. This 'annealing' of the metric can lead to better convergence.
backlog.title: Staged Metric Convergence

backlog.spec: Optimize the logarithm of the radii instead of the radii themselves. This can sometimes help the SLSQP solver handle the wide range of magnitudes and the non-linearities of the distance constraints more smoothly, especially when radii are very small.
backlog.title: Log-Space Radii Search

backlog.spec: Before calling SLSQP, run a brief (e.g., 50 iterations) force-directed simulation where circles repel each other and the boundaries. Use the resulting positions as the `x0` for the SLSQP solver. This pushes the 'random' start into a much more feasible region.
backlog.title: Force-Directed Warm Start

backlog.spec: In the `make_cons` function, instead of returning `d`, return `d - epsilon` where `epsilon` is a small positive value (e.g., 1e-8). This forces the solver to find a packing that is strictly interior to the constraints, providing a buffer against the 1e-10 tolerance check in the harness.
backlog.title: Hard-Constraint Buffer

backlog.spec: After finding a new best packing, perform a few small local searches (e.g., 3-5) by applying a small random perturbation (Gaussian noise with $\sigma=0.02$) to the centers and radii of the best packing found so far, then running a very short SLSQP (e.g., 20 iterations) to see if it settles into a better local optimum.
backlog.title: Basin-Hopping Jittering

backlog.spec: Instead of only shrinking radii during repair, implement an iterative expansion step: if the current packing is valid (no overlaps), try to increase the radii of the circles by a small $\Delta$ until a collision occurs, then back off slightly. This can be repeated for several iterations to 'inflate' the packing.
backlog.title: Radius Expansion Repair

backlog.spec: If the sum of radii is not improving after several SLSQP restarts, identify the smallest circle in the current best packing, remove it, and attempt to re-insert it at a different random location with a slightly larger radius, then run a quick SLSQP to settle.
backlog.title: Small Circle Removal and Re-insertion

backlog.spec: Dynamically adjust the MAX_ITER for each SLSQP call based on the remaining time budget. If only 10% of the total time is left, set MAX_ITER to a small value (e.g., 20); if 80% remains, use a larger value (e.g., 300).
backlog.title: Time-Proportional MAX_ITER

backlog.spec: Optimize the radii in log-space (i.e., solve for $\ln(r)$). This can sometimes help the optimizer handle the wide range of radii sizes more effectively and ensures radii remain positive by construction without needing a hard non-negativity constraint.
backlog.title: Log-Space Radii Search

backlog.spec: Before the first SLSQP call, use a simple force-directed approach: treat circles as particles with a repulsive force proportional to $1/d^2$ (where $d$ is distance between centers). Run this for a fixed number of iterations to 'push' circles away from each other and the boundaries before starting the gradient-based search.
backlog.title: Force-Directed Warm Start

backlog.spec: Perform a two-stage optimization: first, minimize the sum of squared overlaps (a smooth penalty) using a high number of iterations, then switch to the official objective (sum of radii) with hard constraints using the previous result as the starting point.
backlog.title: Staged Metric Convergence

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random radii, sample radii from a power-law distribution (favoring smaller circles) and sort them. Use the largest radii first in the initialization to ensure the most 'difficult' circles are placed first in the search space.
backlog.title: Sorted Radius Initialization

backlog.spec: In the repair step, when updating radii $r_i$ and $r_j$ to resolve an overlap, use a relaxation parameter $\omega \in (1, 2)$ such that $r_{new} = r_{old} + \omega(r_{target} - r_{old})$. This can help accelerate the convergence of the repair loop.
backlog.title: Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR)

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform centers, use a 'jittered grid' or a 'weighted random' approach where points are more likely to be sampled near the boundaries and in the corners, as these are preferred locations for circles in dense packings.
backlog.title: Boundary-Aware Initialization

backlog.spec: Replace the current iterative radius shrinking repair with a SOR-inspired update. In each step of the repair, calculate the required shrinkage factor 's' for all overlapping pairs simultaneously based on the current max overlap, then apply a relaxation factor ϊ (e.g., 1.0 to 1.2) to the update. This helps in 'pushing' the configuration into a valid state more aggressively while avoiding oscillations.
backlog.title: Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR) Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of optimizing radii directly in linear space, optimize their logarithms. This can help the optimizer handle the different scales of large and small radii more effectively and ensures that radii stay positive naturally during the optimization process. The objective function would then involve the sum of the exponentials of the optimized values.
backlog.title: Log-Space Radii Search

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed MAX_ITER, calculate the remaining time in the current restart. Dynamically scale MAX_ITER so that the script spends a consistent amount of time per restart. This ensures that the solver doesn't hang on a single difficult start, maximizing the number of diverse starting points explored.
backlog.title: Time-Proportional MAX_ITER

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP solver starts, sort the initial radii from largest to smallest. Use a greedy heuristic to place the largest circles first (e.g., at random positions or along a spiral) before initializing the smaller circles. This provides a 'better' starting configuration for the local optimizer than a completely uniform random distribution.
backlog.title: Sorted Radius Initialization

backlog.spec: Introduce a global scaling factor α for the radii (sum of radii = α * ∑ r_i). Optimize for the largest possible α such that the circles remain valid. This decouples the relative sizes of the circles from their absolute sizes, potentially smoothing the optimization landscape.
backlog.title: Radius Scaling Architecture

backlog.spec: Instead of hard constraints, use a penalty term: Objective = -(∑ r_i) + λ * (∑ Overlap_ij^2). Start with a small λ and programmatically increase it during the solver's iterations. This 'annealing' of the penalty allows the solver to move through infeasible regions to find better local optima.
backlog.title: Soft Penalty with Gradual Increase

backlog.spec: After the initial repair shrinks the radii to make the packing valid, add a secondary 'inflation' step. Gradually increase all radii by a small epsilon until the first collision occurs (detected via a fast check), then slightly back off. This recovers the 'slack' lost during the initial repair step.
backlog.title: Iterative Radius Expansion Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of optimizing all centers and radii in one large vector, decompose the problem. Alternate between optimizing the centers (x, y) while keeping radii fixed, and then optimizing the radii while keeping centers fixed. This reduces the dimensionality of each sub-problem, which can improve the reliability of the SLSQP solver.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise SLSQP

backlog.spec: Incorporate a basin-hopping approach: after an SLSQP solve, take the resulting packing, apply a large random perturbation (jitter) to the centers, and perform a very short (e.g., 10-20 iterations) 'refinement' SLSQP solve. Repeat this cycle to jump between local optima.
backlog.title: Basin-Hopping Jittering

backlog.spec: Replace the linear wall constraints (e.g., c_x - r >= 0) with a smooth, differentiable barrier function or a higher-order penalty that gets significantly steeper as the circle approaches the boundary. This can provide smoother gradients for the SLSQP solver at the edges of the unit square.
backlog.title: Non-linear Boundary Constraints

backlog.spec: Instead of using a fixed elliptical stretch (s0), sample s0 from a distribution centered at 1.0 with a standard deviation that decreases as the SLSQP solver progresses. Specifically, use a larger stretch (e.g., std dev 0.3) for the first 20% of MAX_ITER to explore the configuration space, and gradually anneal it to 1.0 (std dev 0.0) for the final iterations of the first solve.
backlog.title: Adaptive Stretching

backlog.spec: Replace the constant MAX_ITER with a dynamic value. Calculate the elapsed time since the start of the current `_solve_once` call. Use this to scale the remaining allowed iterations so that the solver is guaranteed to finish near the end of the time limit, rather than potentially using only a fraction of the allotted 30 seconds per solve.
backlog.title: Time-Proportional MAX_ITER

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to slightly favor larger circles. Instead of maximizing the sum of radii, maximize the sum of radii raised to the power of 1.1. This pushes the solver to prioritize placing larger circles, which are more difficult to pack, potentially leading to better overall density in the remaining space.
backlog.title: Weighted Radius Sum Objective

backlog.spec: Instead of one elliptical stretch solve followed by one real-circle solve, perform three successive solves: one with a high stretch (e.g., s=1.3), one with a medium stretch (e.g., s=1.1), and one with the final circle constraints (s=1.0). Each solve uses the result of the previous one as its starting point.
backlog.title: Multi-Stage Stretch sequence

backlog.spec: Maintain the best packing found so far. For 50% of the restarts, instead of sampling purely from the initial distribution, take the best packing found so far and apply a small random jitter to the circle centers (e.g., add Gaussian noise with sigma=0.02) and slightly perturb the radii before starting the SLSQP solve.
backlog.title: Stochastic Restart Jitter

backlog.spec: In the current log-space implementation (v = log(r)), the radii can theoretically grow very large or very small. Add a constraint or a heavy penalty to the objective function to keep radii within a reasonable range (e.g., [0.001, 0.5]) to prevent the solver from pushing circles into 'degenerate' states that are hard to repair.
backlog.title: Log-Space Radius Clipping

backlog.spec: Before starting the SLSQP solve, sort the radii in descending order. Assign the largest radii to the circles whose centers are closest to the center of the unit square, and the smallest radii to those closer to the boundaries. This 'centralized' bias can help the solver find denser packings more reliably.
backlog.title: Greedy Radius Ordering

backlog.spec: In the `_repair` function, instead of scaling both overlapping circles by the same factor `s`, scale the circle with the larger radius by a smaller factor and the smaller circle by a larger factor (e.g., weighted by their relative radii). This preserves the relative size distribution of the circles better during the repair phase.
backlog.title: Dynamic Repair Shrinkage

backlog.spec: Modify the `make_cons` function to include a small safety buffer (e.g., 1e-7) in the distance constraints. Instead of requiring $dist - r_i - r_j \geq 0$, require $dist - r_i - r_j \geq 1e-7$. This ensures that the resulting packing is strictly valid even after floating-point rounding errors occur in the harness's double-precision check.
backlog.title: Constraint Buffer

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call, run a very fast (e.g., 50 iterations) L-BFGS-B optimization that maximizes the sum of radii while using a soft penalty for overlaps (sum of radii + lambda * sum of squared overlaps). Use the result of this soft-penalty run as the starting point for the hard-constraint SLSQP solve.
backlog.title: Soft-Start Penalty Warmup

incumbent.description: Optimise log-radii inside SLSQP (radius = exp(v), so positivity is automatic) and map back to radii on return.

memo:
Helped: only slot 1, running SLSQP first on a randomly stretched (elliptical-metric) problem. It scored -2.6323 and -2.6303, mean -2.6313 over 2 runs, against a baseline of about -2.6280. The gain of about 0.0033 is barely above the noise sd of 0.0023, so it is not firmly confirmed. Slot 22 (three successive stretches) scored -2.6322, no better.

Did not help: penalty methods (slot 0 -2.5921, slot 3 -2.6252) and force-directed relaxation (slot 15 -2.6238). Edge-biased starts and greedy placement both scored -2.6287. Many small tweaks scored -2.6308 to -2.6338 (safety margin, early exit, warm-start, annealing, analytic Jacobian, jitter, smallest-circle removal, shake, screening). All are within noise of the incumbent.

Next: replicate the incumbent to confirm it. Tune the stretch distribution and the share of time spent on stretched starts. Keep SLSQP, avoid penalty and relaxation preprocessing, avoid duplicating aborted ideas, and prefer simple changes.
